lessons.title: Severe Pneumonia: Respiratory Failure & Sepsis
lessons.summary: pneumonia severity is determined by gas exchange and organ dysfunction, not just fever/cough.

sections.title: 1) Presentation
paragraphs: Fever or hypothermia, cough, sputum, pleuritic pain, tachypnea, hypoxemia and focal/diffuse lung findings. Older/immunocompromised patients may present with confusion or weakness.

sections.title: 2) Complications
paragraphs: Sepsis, ARDS, parapneumonic effusion/empyema, necrotizing infection and respiratory failure.

sections.title: 3) Differential
paragraphs: Heart failure, PE, aspiration, COPD/asthma, pneumothorax and noninfectious inflammatory lung disease.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital focus
paragraphs: Oxygen/ventilation support, sepsis/shock recognition, cautious fluids based on phenotype, and early hospital notification in severe hypoxemia/shock.

lessons.title: Dengue: Warning Signs, Critical Phase & Fluid Precision
lessons.summary: dengue can worsen around defervescence when plasma leakage begins; too much fluid can also harm.

sections.title: 1) Phases
paragraphs: Febrile phase → possible critical phase near defervescence → recovery. Plasma leakage can cause hemoconcentration, effusions and shock.

sections.title: 2) Warning signs
paragraphs: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding, lethargy/restlessness, fluid accumulation, hepatomegaly and laboratory trends can indicate risk.

sections.title: 3) Shock
paragraphs: Narrow pulse pressure, cool extremities and delayed refill can precede hypotension. Fluid resuscitation must be carefully reassessed because leak later reverses.

sections.title: 4) Avoid harm
paragraphs: Avoid NSAIDs/aspirin because of bleeding risk; IM injections and unnecessary invasive procedures may be problematic in thrombocytopenia.

sources.label: WHO dengue guidance / local Thai protocols

lessons.title: Antimicrobial Thinking in Emergency Care
lessons.summary: early antibiotics can be lifesaving in serious bacterial infection, but stewardship requires correct indication, source and reassessment.

sections.title: 1) Infection is not always bacterial
paragraphs: Viral, fungal, parasitic and noninfectious inflammatory syndromes mimic bacterial sepsis. Obtain useful cultures/testing when it does not meaningfully delay urgent therapy.

sections.title: 2) Time-sensitive severe infection
paragraphs: Septic shock/meningitis and selected severe infections require rapid antimicrobial therapy; exact timing/regimen depends on syndrome and guideline.

sections.title: 3) Source control
paragraphs: Drain abscess, relieve obstruction, remove infected device, operate on perforation—antibiotics alone cannot fix some sources.

sections.title: 4) Stewardship
paragraphs: Use local antibiogram/protocol, allergies, renal function and previous resistant organisms; de-escalate when data permit.
